title: What Does RL Post-Training Teach Text-to-Image Models? A Skill-Wise Analysis of Flow-GRPO
abstract: arXiv:2611.33316v1 Announce Type: cross  Abstract: Reinforcement learning (RL) post-training has become a standard way to improve text-to-image flow models: Flow-GRPO lifts the GenEval score of SD3.5-M from 0.63 to 0.95, a gain read as the model having learned compositional generation. We ask how much of that gain the base model's own samples already contained, by measuring pass@k over shared noise seeds, one skill at a time, before and after RL, on prompts never used in training. The answer differs by skill. On four of GenEval's six skills, where 32 base samples already solve almost every prompt, the gain is sharpening: one post-trained sample is worth 4 to 10 base samples, and pass@32 barely moves. On spatial relations it is unlocking: pass@32 rises from 0.69 to 1.00, 128 base samples do not match one post-trained sample, and prompts the base model never solved in 32 samples are solved 93% of the time, as often as those it solved. The benchmark average, 31 base samples per post-train

translated_title: RL后训练究竟教会了文生图模型什么？——对Flow-GRPO的技能维度分析
translated_abstract: 强化学习（RL）后训练已成为改进文生图流模型的标准方法：Flow-GRPO将SD3.5-M的GenEval分数从0.63提升至0.95，这一提升被解读为模型学会了组合式生成。我们通过在共享噪声种子上测量pass@k（逐项技能、在RL前后、使用训练中从未出现过的提示）来探究这一提升中有多少是基础模型自身的样本早已具备的。答案因技能而异。在GenEval六项技能中的四项上——其中32个基础样本已能解决几乎所有的提示——这种提升属于“锐化”：一个后训练样本的价值相当于4到10个基础样本，而pass@32几乎没有变化。在空间关系技能上，这种提升属于“解锁”：pass@32从0.69升至1.00，128个基础样本也抵不上一个后训练样本，且基础模型在32个样本中从未解决过的提示，被后训练模型以93%的比例解决——与其原本就能解决的提示频率相当。就基准测试的平均值而言，一个后训练样本相当于31个基础样本（原文在此处截断）。
tldr: 本文通过逐技能测量pass@k发现，Flow-GRPO后训练对文生图模型的提升大多是“锐化”（放大基础模型本已具备的能力），只有在空间关系上才是真正“解锁”了新能力，因此基准分数的提升在很大程度上夸大了模型真正学到的东西。
en_tdlr: By measuring pass@k skill by skill, this paper shows that Flow-GRPO's gains in text-to-image models are mostly "sharpening" (amplifying abilities the base model already had), while only spatial relations show genuine "unlocking" of new capabilities, meaning benchmark improvements largely overstate what RL post-training actually teaches.
